tasks.short: Lecture on accounting, marketing and operations.

steps.what: Read the posted lecture line for this session.
Prepare and deliver lectures to undergraduate or graduate students on these topics.

tasks.design: The business teacher still prepares and delivers lectures to undergraduate or graduate students on these topics. A lecture line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with course, topic, session date, place and the author's name, so the hunt for that sheet is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The lecture line sat on a paper sheet, so the teacher hunted it before the session.
tasks.enabler_now: The course file already holds a lecture line. Showing course, topic, session date, place and the author's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: How to teach the topic in the room is the lecture. A posted line does not deliver it.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher hears the class and refuses a line that does not name this session.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the lecture. Less time goes to hunting a sheet. The teacher still delivers it.

reach.task: Post the lecture line before the session.
reach.learn: The line needs course, topic, session date, place and the author's name, or the teacher reads the paper sheet.

reach.task: Leave this session with this teacher.
reach.learn: Delivering the lecture is this teacher's own talk. It is not a send.

reach.task: Stay in the class while the teacher lectures.
reach.learn: The student does not deliver the lecture in the teacher's place, and does not file a note.

evidence.claim: Preparing and delivering the lecture stays with the business teacher. A posted lecture line can be a shorter read. The lecture itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
Evaluating learning outcomes, and detecting cheating in tests, are high-risk uses. This design does not evaluate outcomes, does not detect cheating, and does not draft the lecture.
Inferring emotion in education is prohibited. This design does not infer emotion from the class or from the teacher.

The posted line is a course, a topic, a session date, a place and an author's name. It is not a recording and not a grade. National rules vary. The digest names the Netherlands for the education and works-council laws.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is only preparing and delivering lectures to undergraduate or graduate students on topics such as financial accounting, principles of marketing, and operations management. Grading, moderating a discussion and preparing materials sit outside it. The programme coordinator posts the line before the session.

Structured input: one lecture line in the {DOCS} with course, topic, session date, place and the author's name. The line is the session topic, not a recording and not a grade. If the line is missing or free text, the teacher reads the paper sheet and that read is not shorter.

The teacher still prepares and delivers the lecture in the room. Nothing is recorded by a machine, sent, or committed. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. A recording or a slide file sent outside the organisation would be its own step, with a gate on the final version. That step is not in this design, and it is not folded into the lecture. The prior that the lecture is a draft for someone else, or a send outside the organisation, is refused: it is the teacher's own talk in the room, and it is a write inside the organisation.
A model is not used. Existing system runtime is not the teacher's time. The design does not evaluate learning outcomes, detect cheating, infer emotion, monitor the teacher, or file a note.
unknowns: Whether this course file already has course, topic, session date, place and a name, or only a paper sheet.
Whether the site later wants a recording of the lecture. This design does not send one.
research_questions: Who posts the lecture line, the programme coordinator or the teacher?
What share of sessions start with no line the teacher can read?

already_counted.description: Reading a missing or free-text lecture sheet by hand, inside the remaining read.

incremental.description: Checking that the lecture line still names this session, course, topic, session date, place and an author.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the lecture line is often missing or free text, so the teacher still hunts the paper sheet and the read is not shorter. High: most lines carry course, topic, session date, place and an author's name, and only that hunt shrinks. The lecture stays. The high stays under the net after the field check.

evidence.claim: Evaluating and grading class work, assignments and papers stays with the business teacher. A posted marking line can be a shorter read. The grading itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
Evaluating learning outcomes, and detecting cheating in tests, are high-risk uses. This design does not grade with a model and does not detect cheating.
A grade set solely by a model is likely a decision based solely on automated processing. This design does not set a grade by a model.
The examiner appointed by the examination board sets the result, and only that board sanctions fraud. This design leaves the judgement with the teacher and does not file the result or sanction fraud.
A system able to monitor staff, such as a per-examiner marking dashboard, needs works council consent. This design does not add a dashboard and does not monitor the teacher.

The posted line is a course, an assignment name, a criteria name, a date and an author's name. It is not the student's paper and not a grade. National rules vary. The digest names the Netherlands for the education and works-council laws.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is only evaluating and grading students class work, assignments and papers. Lecturing, moderating a discussion and preparing materials sit outside it. The programme coordinator posts the line before the set.

Structured input: one marking line in the {DOCS} with course, assignment name, criteria name, date and the author's name. The line is the criteria topic, not the student's paper, not a score and not a staff record. If the line is missing or free text, the teacher reads the paper sheet and that read is not shorter.

The teacher still evaluates the work and sets the judgement. Nothing is recorded by a machine, sent, or committed. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. Lodging the result with the examination board, or publishing the grade in the course record, would be its own step, with a gate on the final version. That step is not in this design, and it is not folded into the grading. The prior that a model grades these papers is refused.

A model is not used. Existing system runtime is not the teacher's time. The design does not evaluate learning outcomes with a tool, detect cheating, add a marking dashboard, monitor the teacher, or file a result.
